newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end uneven in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end uneven in thin trade.

text.p: Thin trade prevailed and CME lumber futures ranged on both sides of Friday's close before ending unevely lower, traders said.
Lumber closed $1.00 per tbf higher to $2.00 lower with May off $0.10 at $394.60 and July off $1.70 at $393.30 per tbf.

Futures showed little direction and only May briefly ran up for a large gain on a buy order before quickly turning back down. The weak tone to cash weighed on the market while the discount to cash limited losses, traders said.
Cash spruce fell $11 last week to $399 and cash sources put prices now at $385 to $395 per tbf.
The U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes in March down 2.5 percent to an 813,000 unit annual rate.
The report had little effect on the market as sales were in the range of expectations, traders added.
